title: Drummers' volume, baggage costs and the bass drum
summary: Modern drum sets need a whole platform, cost $400 in excess baggage to Europe, and Garland wants to hear his bass over the bass drum.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: And it seems as though you may have friends who are drummers, but they often give us trouble with the volume, they often play very loud and you were saying while we were switching the tape over, something very interesting, that it seems as though the older drummers made more sounds with less drums, than today, when they have so many --
What'd you say, it takes a whole platform for the drums today?
Take the whole platform to set the drums up. We had the man -- we was going over to Europe and the many had so many drums there -- he was overweight on the
had to pay $400.00 extra, you know, for --
Over -- and I had to pay it. I didn't have to pay it, but I paid it. Loan him the money. The manager wasn't there, you understand, and we was on our way back from England, went to Los Angeles.
Do you like -- excuse me, when the drummer plays the bass drum, four beats, do you like four beats on the bass drum?
Oh, yeah. One-two-three-four, one-two-three-four. You got it, that's that bass drum, boom-boom-boom, boom-boom-boom. And he's sweet, sweeping, choo-choo-choo --
Lot of these drummers blam-blam-blam. They blast too much.
Almost double forte to begin with and double forte going out.
Uh-huh. Ah, do you like to blend with the sound of the bass drum, your bass?
Okay, so in other words, they shouldn't play too loud on the bass drums?
Uh-huh, okay, so you want to hear your bass over the bass drum?
